How to use this sheet

  1. Print the PDF and keep it near where you'd reach for gout medication.
  2. When a flare starts, log the date and joint — write while it's fresh, not later.
  3. Rate peak severity (0–10) and count how many days it took to resolve.
  4. In the 'preceding' column, note the last 24–48 hours honestly: meals, alcohol, water, whether you missed any daily medication.
  5. After several flares, patterns often become obvious. Bring the diary to your doctor along with any uric acid readings.

Questions

Is this diary really free?

Yes. The PDF is free to download and print — no sign-up, no email.

What if I only get flares once or twice a year?

That's exactly when a paper diary helps. Memory of what preceded a flare a year ago is unreliable; a written note at the time is honest data your future self can use.

Should I record every twinge or only real flares?

Judgment call — but many people find that recording anything that felt like the start of a flare (even ones that fizzled) is useful, because near-misses can reveal the same triggers.

Is there an app version?

Yes — GoutLog for iPhone logs flares, meals, uric acid, and hydration together, then highlights which foods or gaps in medication appear most often before your worse flares. Core is free, no account needed, data stays on your device.
